To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of deep learning for 3D data is possible, (2) it is possible to learn from incomplete and noisy data, (3) it is possible and useful to learn a generative model for 3D shapes, and (4) it is possible that the learned model can be used to generate 3D shapes from 3D point clouds.
we propose a novel deep learning approach to learn a generative model of shapes from raw point clouds.

1) we introduce an unsupervised learning framework to learn a deep generative model that captures the shape distribution of a class of objects; 2) we introduce the concept of a deep generative volumetric shape autoencoder, which is a deep generative neural network that is able to reconstruct 3D shapes from a 3D voxel representation; 3) we show that the learned deep generative model of shapes can be used to generate novel shapes that are similar to real shapes
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can we learn to reconstruct 3D objects from incomplete and noisy depth maps?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a deep learning approach that learns a volumetric shape representation of everyday objects from noisy and partial scans.
we are interested in the question how we can learn to reconstruct the 3D geometry of objects without having to label them.
we propose a new deep learning framework for reconstructing 3D shapes of objects in the wild.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can learn the underlying shape distribution of objects without the need to label the shapes with their class labels.
deep learning can be used to learn shape priors from unstructured point clouds and that these can be used to reconstruct complete and noise-free 3D models from partial or noisy data.
